title: GEFEG BatteryPass-Ready longlist attributes
authority: GEFEG (publication and validation channel for the Battery Pass Consortium)
usedFor: A regulation-cited attribute catalogue, not just the residual gap after the SAMM comparisons — see finding.
source: https://thebatterypass.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026_BatteryPass-Ready_DataAttributeLongList_v1.3.xlsx — fetched directly (not the survey's mirror) and read (all 772 unique cell strings scanned).
finding: No IRI anywhere in the file — confirms the survey's own namespace (`https://ref.openepcis.io/vocab/batterypass-ready/1.3#`) is its own coinage, not GEFEG's; the prior finding about that stands. No licence statement anywhere in the file either — `licence: null` is confirmed correct, not merely unestablished. **Correction to the prior `usedFor` framing**: this is not a narrow residual list of attributes SAMM omits — it's a comprehensive attribute catalogue built on DIN DKE SPEC 99100, with one row per data attribute carrying: which battery categories it's mandatory/voluntary for, its regulation reference (Battery Regulation, ESPR, or JTC-24 standardization), unit, data format, Battery Regulation Annex XIII / Art. 77 access-rights tier, static-vs-dynamic behaviour, and model-vs-individual-battery granularity. That last set of columns is exactly the citation work our own `Option`-field discipline requires ("add as Option, with the citation") — this document has, per attribute, already done it.
nextStep: This is now the highest-value single source for the gap list already opened by `batterypass-samm` and `catena-x-battery-pass` — cross-reference each gap found there (hazardous substances, warranty, conformity/labelling, end-of-life/safety, ESG disclosure) against this longlist's regulation-reference column before going to the OJ text directly; it will likely name the exact article for most of them. Terms stay ours to name, never the survey's coined IRI — the regulation reference is what's citable, not GEFEG's attribute label.
